name: Lick Observatory CCD data acquisition system
description: Lick Observatory used a programmable controller to operate several types of charge-coupled detector. The controller digitized signals near the detector and sent the data over a serial link to a UNIX computer for acquisition and online analysis.

places.note: Lick Observatory, University of California, Santa Cruz.

date.basis: Month of the Optical Engineering issue. The components had already been put into use.

events.statement: Robinson and colleagues published the design and observational uses of the standard Lick CCD data acquisition system. A separate photometer paper reported use of much of the same hardware.

evidence.supports: Names the observatory, describes the system and reports operation with three instruments.
Identifies components drawn from the standard Lick system and documents a working installation.

earliest_record.rationale: The 1987 publication documents the UNIX-based system later cited in Berkeley's detector characterization. The date of initial operation is unresolved.

unresolved.note: Tod Lauer's August 1981 report documents a PDP-8 system at Lick. The extent of hardware or software retained by the UNIX system described in 1987 needs further source work.
